final_task_tree.title: Figure out a training plan for my dog
final_task_tree.description:
Rescue border collie mix, 14 months. Pulls hard on the leash and barks at every other dog on walks. South Bay, California; I can do evenings and weekends.

Three things only:
1. Whether to hire a trainer or do it myself.
2. If hiring — two or three local options with real prices.
3. A week-by-week plan for the first four weeks.

Don't research anything beyond those three.

comments.body:
Picking this up. Scoping to exactly the three things you asked for: (1) DIY vs. hire, (2) 2–3 South Bay options with real prices, (3) a 4-week week-by-week plan. Nothing beyond that — no nutrition, no gear rabbit holes, no crate/separation stuff.

Building the subtask tree now, then researching.
comments.author: agent

subtasks.title: Decide: DIY vs. hired trainer for leash pulling + dog reactivity
subtasks.description: Determine whether a 14-month rescue border collie mix with (a) hard leash pulling and (b) barking at every dog on walks is a DIY case or a hire-a-pro case. Two behaviours, so judge separately — loose-leash walking and reactivity are not the same difficulty. Output: a clear recommendation with the reasoning, written into this description, plus the specific red flags that would change the answer.

subtasks.title: Find South Bay trainers who handle leash reactivity, with real prices
subtasks.description: Find 2–3 South Bay CA (Sunnyvale / Santa Clara / San Jose / Mountain View / Campbell) trainers or behaviour consultants who explicitly work on leash reactivity with positive-reinforcement / LIMA methods. Must capture: actual price per session or package price, what the package includes, format (in-home / private / class), evening+weekend availability, and phone/email. No 'contact for pricing' entries unless nothing else exists.

subtasks.title: Verify credentials and method for each shortlisted trainer
subtasks.description: For each trainer on the shortlist, confirm the certification letters (CPDT-KA, KPA-CTP, CDBC, CBCC-KA, VSA-CDT, or DACVB for a vet behaviourist) and confirm they do not use prong/e-collar/'balanced' methods. Reactivity is fear/arousal-based, so aversive tools are the specific thing to screen out. Record findings against each trainer.

subtasks.title: Write the week-by-week plan for weeks 1–4
subtasks.description: Build a 4-week plan that fits evenings + weekends only. Must run two parallel tracks: loose-leash walking and dog reactivity (engage-disengage / counter-conditioning at distance). Include per-session length, how many sessions a week, what 'passing' looks like before advancing, and where in the South Bay to practise at safe distance. Keep it realistic for someone with a job.
